setups.label: Plain DuckDB
setups.title: Plain DuckDB is enough
setups.body: You are one person on one machine and you do not need remote access or history. DuckDB alone does this well. Come back to QoD when others need to connect.

setups.label: qod serve on files
setups.title: qod serve on your files
setups.body: One secure gateway over data you already have. TLS, auth and access control are on by default. No Postgres or Docker to set up.

setups.label: qod serve + Iceberg
setups.title: qod serve with your Iceberg catalog
setups.body: Keep Iceberg as your table format. QoD attaches your REST catalog as a federated source, and the same RBAC, tenants and routing apply to its tables. Undrop, rollback and author stamping are DuckLake only.

setups.label: qod serve on DuckLake
setups.title: qod serve on DuckLake
setups.body: The full platform: a DuckLake warehouse on Postgres and object storage, with time travel, tags, undrop, rollback, author stamping and managed maintenance. Iceberg and other sources can still be attached next to it.

reasons.duckdb: Only you query the data, on one machine, with no history needs.
reasons.history: Undo, time travel and audit come with DuckLake.

reasons.ducklake: Your data is already in DuckLake.
reasons.iceberg: Your tables stay in Iceberg; QoD attaches the catalog.
reasons.files: QoD serves the files you already have.

notes.text: Evaluating? Start with uvx qod serve --demo, then move to this setup.
A single .duckdb file is served by one node only. Parquet, csv or S3 prefixes scale out.
If you later need undrop, rollback or author stamping, those require DuckLake tables.
Your Iceberg catalog is attached as a federated source: RBAC applies, but DuckLake history features do not.
Several nodes belong on your servers or cloud account. Try it single node on your laptop first.
